texts.orig: Q: I'm joining a new team that has a history of underperformance and lots of execution issues. What advice do you have for joining a turnaround situation like this one?
texts.text: Q: I'm joining a new team that has a history of underperformance and lots of execution issues. What advice do you have for joining a turnaround situation like this one?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: I’ve been in this spot a couple of times, and as painful as these situations are, they’re also chock full of potential. The risk that you take on (of failing, of slowing down your career by being bogged down on a sub-par team) is also the fuel that catapults your career forward if you can pull this off.

The risk that you take on (of failing, of slowing down your career by being bogged down on a sub-par team) is also the fuel that catapults your career forward if you can pull this off.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: My advice is to lean into this opportunity. Show your team, your manager, and your peers that they can count on you to make difficult decisions, create necessary change, and deliver impact in tough situations.
texts.text: My advice is to lean into this opportunity. Show your team, your manager, and your peers that they can count on you to make difficult decisions, create necessary change, and deliver impact in tough situations.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: To help, here are five tips for taking advantage of this opportunity:
texts.text: To help, here are five tips for taking advantage of this opportunity:

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 1. Set clear expectations with your manager 👀
texts.text: 1. Set clear expectations with your manager 👀

texts.label: text
texts.orig: It’s critical that your manager, and other influential leaders, understand the situation that you are being put into. It’s likely for the next 6-12 months you’ll drive less business impact than you had previously, and that some team members will become upset with you (particularly if you implement difficult changes). Make sure your manager and other leaders understand this when you’re coming into it. This way, when you succeed, it’ll be all the more impressive.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 5. Find your allies 🤝
texts.text: 5. Find your allies 🤝

texts.label: text
texts.orig: When you determine what needs to change (e.g. a process, a goal, a person), you’ll find some people are 100% aligned and ready to roll, some people completely disagree, and the rest are unsure but willing to give it a shot. Figure out early-on who’s going to back you up, and who you’re going to have to convince. Do you need buy-in from managers outside of the team, or can you take care of things internally? Do you need a “come to Jesus” moment with the team, or can the changes be made gradually.
